block coordinates translated into client space the way PaneView does,
since the editor and the host live in different scroll coordinate
systems.

`view.scrollDOM` and nothing else changed, tw1 fails at 314px off centre
and tw2 fails on its precondition at 184px; restored, both pass.

_comment_333_to_334: 333 -> 334 (myne-md/myne#555). One scenario, wc1
(`window-close-flush.e2e.ts`): closing the window flushes unsaved work.
Two app launches, the second a cold start on the tree the first left
behind.
It needs `python3`, now named on BOTH seats (`e2e/Dockerfile` and the two
`.woodpecker.yml` E2E steps) so `check-e2e-toolchain.mjs` covers it.
THE BULLET'S PREMISE IS WRONG, and the wrong version PASSES. It says
`xdotool windowclose` sends WM_DELETE_WINDOW. It does not — it calls
XDestroyWindow, so GTK raises no `delete-event`, tao raises no
`CloseRequested`, and Editor.tsx's handler never runs. The app still
exits, which is what makes it expensive: every outward sign of a graceful
close is present and none of the graceful behaviour happened.
Measured twice rather than reasoned. `strings` over the image's
`libxdo.so.3` contains neither WM_DELETE_WINDOW nor WM_PROTOCOLS; and a
probe write injected into the close handler did not land after an
`xdotool windowclose`, then landed once the close became a real
ClientMessage. `wmctrl -c` is also wrong here — it asks the WINDOW
MANAGER, and under xvfb there is none.
So the close goes through `e2e/support/wm-delete-window.py`, ~20 lines of
Xlib via ctypes.
BOTH HALVES PROVE THE DISK WAS STALE FIRST, because the end state is also
what an ordinary autosave produces: the note body is read off disk after
typing and asserted to LACK the new sentence (and the editor buffer
asserted to have it, since `not on disk` is also true of text never
typed), and the workspace descriptor is asserted not to name the note
opened this session.
An earlier version of the workspace half was BACKWARDS twice over: it
planted a marker with `workspace_write` and asserted it SURVIVED, but
that command writes straight to disk (it survives a SIGKILL and says
nothing about a close) and `persistWorkspace()` OVERWRITES it — so the
assertion passed exactly when the handler had not run.
What the workspace half does NOT isolate, also measured: removing
`persistWorkspace()` alone does not fail it. Two independent paths persist
the layout on a graceful exit — that one, and the backend's
`RunEvent::ExitRequested` arm flushing the staged container (which exists
because Cmd+Q fires ExitRequested and never `onCloseRequested`). The
assertion is therefore worded as the user-visible property rather than as
one mechanism. It still discriminates the subject: under
`xdotool windowclose` NEITHER path ran.
Discriminator verified: removing `await flushAll()` from the close handler
fails the note-body half by name while the workspace half still passes.

_comment_334_to_335: 334 -> 335 (myne-md/myne#555). One scenario, rms1
(`rtl-mirror-sweep.e2e.ts`): the chrome actually MIRRORS in an RTL
locale, measured side by side.
It executes wherever the suite does: one seeded vault, no sidecar, no
feature flag, no network.
THE GAP IT FILLS. `rtl-layout.e2e.ts` (rtl1) pins the CONTRACT —
picking an RTL locale flips `<html dir>` live, and a mixed-script title
stays `<bdi>`-isolated. It does not check that anything MOVED, and a
tree that sets `dir="rtl"` and lays out identically satisfies every
assertion in it. That is the realistic regression: one physical `left`
or `marginLeft` in an inline style is unreachable to a
logical-property mirror, permanently, and the chrome flips around it.
